chunks: The venerable Shaykh Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Musa ibn Babawayh al-Qummi (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba from Hamdan ibn Sulayman from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Salih ibn 'Uqba from 'Alqama ibn Muhammad al-Hadrami from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of God (may God bless him and his family) said: God, exalted is His majesty, said:

God, exalted is His majesty, said: My servants! All of you are misguided except those I have guided. All of you are poor except those I have enriched. All of you are sinners except those I have protected.

key_terms.أغنيته: I have enriched — divine provision and sufficiency, removing need through God's grace
key_terms.عبادي: My servants — God's address to all of creation, expressing the servant-Lord relationship
key_terms.عصمته: I have protected — divine protection ('isma) from sin, theologically connected to the infallibility of Prophets and Imams
key_terms.هديته: I have guided — divine guidance (hidaya), the source of all right direction

ai.seo_question: What did God say about guidance, provision, and protection of His servants in this hadith qudsi?
ai.summary: This is a hadith qudsi (sacred tradition) — a divine utterance conveyed through the Prophet Muhammad (S) via a chain tracing through the Shi'a Imams back to Imam al-Sadiq (AS). In it, God addresses all of humanity with three parallel declarations: that all are astray save those He guides, all are impoverished save those He provides for, and all are sinful save those He protects from sin. The threefold structure emphasizes the absolute dependence of creation upon divine grace for spiritual guidance, material provision, and moral integrity. The concept of 'isma (protection from sin) in the final clause carries special theological significance in Shi'a Islam, as it underpins the doctrine of the infallibility of the Prophets and Imams.
